title: Resolve misattributed usage for sub-accounts after API key rotation and credential fallthrough
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are observing incorrect tenant attribution for a subset of requests after API key rotation when requests fall through to a parent/workspace mapping. Tokens and API usage that should be attributed to sub-accounts are being assigned to parent orgs or the original owner across multiple customers, leading to billing inaccuracies and quota enforcement issues.

Reproduction steps (observed in prod):
1) Customer creates a sub-account with an API key A mapped to workspace W-sub.
2) Customer rotates key (key B replaces key A) via the Keys service. Rotation completes but some long-lived cache entries (rate limiter, usage attribution cache) still reference the old key->workspace mapping.
3) Requests arrive during the small window where the mapping is inconsistent. The request lookup falls back to parent mapping logic and attributes usage to the parent org or fallback workspace.
4) Result: sub-account usage not billed to correct sub-account, and quotas/rate limits applied to wrong tenant.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by sampling logs):
- The attribution path queries a three-layer lookup: local cache -> persistent key map -> fallback mapping.
- During rotation we perform an asynchronous update to the persistent mapping and emit an invalidation message. However, the rate limiter and the in-memory attribution cache do not subscribe to the invalidation channel fast enough; they keep an old key->workspace pairing for up to 90s.
- The fallback path is permissive: when key->workspace lookup fails it attempts a parent org match rather than rejecting. This permissive fallthrough was implemented earlier to handle legacy guest keys but now causes misattribution during transient states.

Scope & impact:
- Affects customers that rotate API keys frequently and use sub-accounting features.
- Estimated affected requests: ~0.1% of all token events in the last 7 days; concentrated in 12 enterprise customers (support ticket correlation).
- Customer impact: incorrect billing line-items, potentially double-billed parent orgs, and incorrect quota enforcement leading to unexpected throttling.

Short-term mitigations (already applied):
- Emergency change: reduced cache TTL for attribution cache from 2m -> 5s (rolled back to 30s for performance). Deployed to us-west and eu-west on 2025-02-16 03:10 UTC.
- Manual audit and back-billing script created to retroactively reassign misattributed tokens for affected customers (run pending legal/finance signoff).
- Added alert: grafana alert billing.attribution.fallthrough_rate > 0.5% (firing since 2025-02-14).

Proposed long-term fix (design & engineering):
1) Atomic swap for key mappings: extend Keys service to produce a versioned mapping and require consumers to perform compare-and-swap updates rather than async invalidations.
2) Stronger invariants in attribution service: when a key->workspace lookup returns stale/unknown, fail-safe to rejecting attribution rather than permissive parent fallthrough. Add a configurable opt-in fallback flag for legacy flows.
3) Subscription-based cache invalidation: ensure rate limiter and attribution caches subscribe to a durable invalidation channel (Kafka/Redis stream) and perform immediate invalidation on rotation events.
4) Add end-to-end integration tests simulating rotations under load, verifying no misattribution in < 1s windows.
5) Backfill pipeline: continue building an idempotent backfill that maps misattributed events to correct customers and produces a reconciliation report for Finance.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (safety): enforce conservative TTL and enable enhanced logging (complete).
- Phase 2 (stronger invariant): change fallback behavior to 'reject->log' behind a runtime flag and run in shadow mode for 48h in staging then canary in prod (estimated 2 weeks).
- Phase 3 (atomic mapping & durable invalidation): deploy Keys service versioned mapping and update consumers (4 weeks).
- Phase 4 (monitor & backfill): run recon, customer communication, and finalize billing adjustments (2 weeks after Phase 3).

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Target: attribution_misassign_rate < 0.01% across all regions.
- Dashboards to monitor: grafana.d/billing/usage-attribution, rate_limiter.cache_miss_rate, keys.rotation_lag_seconds.
- Alerts: escalate to oncall if misassign_rate > 0.1% for 10m.

QA/test plan:
- Unit tests for attribution lookup logic and fallback behavior.
- Integration tests simulating key rotation bursts and asserting no misattribution.
- Load test in staging with synthetic keys and a mix of rotating and non-rotating clients.

Docs & comms:
- Update troubleshooting guide in Confluence and public KB on how rotations are handled.
- Prepare customer outreach templates for affected accounts (billing and CS to review).
comments: 2025-02-12 - Triage: Issue opened by Aisha. Initial priority set to P0 after confirming billing discrepancies in production logs.
2025-02-13 - Investigation: Liam reproduced mapping TTL mismatch in staging and identified cache invalidation lag in rate limiter process. Collected traces and sample request ids.

2025-02-14 - Mitigation: Deployed emergency TTL reduction in us-west and eu-west. Enabled extra logging to capture misassign events. Created retroactive backfill script (draft) at https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1248.
2025-02-18 - Design review: Product and Finance signed off on backfill approach; proposed atomic mapping design reviewed by infra (notes in Confluence link).
2025-02-22 - PRs: Opened change to attribution logic to reject permissive fallthrough behind runtime flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1273. Running e2e in staging.
2025-02-25 - Next steps: Complete durable invalidation hookup (Kafka) and plan phased rollout. Preparation for customer communications in parallel.
